message.content: The largest confirmed exoplanet discovered so far has a mass of roughly 20 Jupiter masses (about 0.02 solar masses). It’s often cited as **HD 100546 b**, orbiting the young star HD 100546. This object sits at the upper end of the planetary mass range and borders on the definition of a brown dwarf, but it remains the most massive “planet‑sized” body we’ve found to date.
